indigo.purpose: Department identity color. Owns the navigation rail solidly in both appearances; the system's one accent for selection/primary/links.

coral.purpose: Overdue items, destructive actions, error alerts. --red-fill (#c0303c) stays fixed across appearances for white-text surfaces; --red text token is #c0303c light / #f7636e dark.

apricot.purpose: Due-soon status, warning alerts, the rail's marker color (--rail-marker). Also darkened to #9c5116 for light-mode text; dark-mode text uses the raw tint.

aqua.purpose: Available/returned status and reservation info. Darkened to #0f6c72 for light-mode text; dark-mode text uses the raw tint.

violet.purpose: The roster/people lane (Members count on the librarian dashboard). An entity class, not urgency.

display.purpose: Toolbar h1, hero/auth headlines. Fraunces at opsz 72 / SOFT 22 / WONK 1.

headline.purpose: Panel/section h2; member phone shell's decorative large-title (aria-hidden).

body.purpose: Controls, table cells, form fields, paragraphs -- the system's true base size.

label.purpose: Column headers, sidebar section headings, field labels, badge text.

mono.purpose: ISBNs, call numbers, accession lines, dates, counts -- anything that must align in a fixed column.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Resting panels, cards, stat tiles, book cards, slips (light). Dark: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.40), 0 0 0 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.06).

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Hover-lifted cards/stats/slips, the auth card (light). Dark: 0 3px 14px rgba(0,0,0,0.48), 0 0 0 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.07).

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Menus, confirmation sheets, the open mobile drawer (light). Dark: 0 18px 52px rgba(0,0,0,0.62), 0 0 0 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.10).

shadows.name: glass-shadow
shadows.purpose: The frosted glass icon button only.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.purpose: Button :active squash -- reinforces physicality (0.975 on phone tab bar items).

breakpoints.name: shell
breakpoints.purpose: Rail becomes overlay drawer with scrim; tables stack; member shell switches to bottom tab bar with crossfading large-title.

breakpoints.name: row-stack
breakpoints.purpose: List rows (.row-item) drop their status/actions group to its own line so book titles keep a usable measure. Content-driven, not a device class.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Stat grid drops to 2 columns; hero padding tightens; searchbar stacks vertically; slip stub narrows from 92px to 78px.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one filled, indigo button in the system -- reserved for the primary action on a page or panel.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary" type="button"><svg class="ds-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.7" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></svg>Add Book</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 7px; padding: 7px 15px; min-height: 34px; font: 550 14px Archivo, -apple-system, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -0.004em; color: #fff; background: var(--accent-fill, #292168); border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--r-sm, 5px); box-shadow: 0 1px 1.5px rgba(26,21,65,0.08); cursor: pointer; white-space: nowrap; transition: background 180ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--accent-hover, #3d3490); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #292168); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 3px; } .ds-btn-primary .ds-icon { width: 16px; height: 16px; flex: none; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The default button shape -- neutral fill, hairline indigo-tinted border. Used everywhere a primary button isn't warranted.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 7px; padding: 7px 15px; min-height: 34px; font: 550 14px Archivo, -apple-system, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -0.004em; color: var(--fg, #1a1541); background: var(--bg-raised, #fff); border: 1px solid var(--separator-strong, rgba(41,33,104,0.22)); border-radius: var(--r-sm, 5px); box-shadow: 0 1px 1.5px rgba(26,21,65,0.08); cursor: pointer; white-space: nowrap; transition: background 180ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), border-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--bg-hover, rgba(41,33,104,0.045)); border-color: var(--accent, #292168); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: scale(0.98); background: var(--bg-active, rgba(41,33,104,0.085)); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #292168); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 3px; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: A rounded status pill recolored per semantic role (accent/coral/apricot/aqua) but always the same pill shape.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; padding: 3px 9px; font: 700 11px Archivo, -apple-system, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; border-radius: 999px; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-badge-red { background: rgba(247,99,110,0.16); color: var(--red, #c0303c); } .ds-badge-accent { background: var(--accent-soft, rgba(41,33,104,0.09)); color: var(--accent, #292168); } .ds-badge-green { background: rgba(93,203,209,0.22); color: var(--green, #0f6c72); }

components.name: Category Badge
components.description: Book-category identity badge, hue-derived from the category string, confined to the aqua-through-indigo brand arc so a category reads as a stable color everywhere.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-block; vertical-align: middle; padding: 3px 9px; font: 700 11px Archivo, -apple-system, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; border-radius: 999px; max-width: 22ch; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-badge-category { background: hsl(230 55% 95%); color: hsl(230 75% 26%); }

components.name: Stat Tile
components.description: The primary dashboard card -- a linkable tile with a top-edge status rule and a large Fraunces value, lifting slightly on hover.
components.html: Overdue4
components.css: .ds-stat { display: block; position: relative; background: var(--bg-content, #fff); border-radius: var(--r-lg, 12px); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(26,21,65,0.07), 0 0 0 1px rgba(41,33,104,0.06); padding: 16px 18px 18px; overflow: hidden; text-decoration: none; transition: transform 180ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), box-shadow 180ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-stat:hover { box-shadow: 0 3px 12px rgba(26,21,65,0.10), 0 0 0 1px rgba(41,33,104,0.06); transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-stat::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: 0; height: 3px; } .ds-stat-red::after { background: #f7636e; } .ds-stat-top { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; color: var(--fg-secondary, #5b5480); font: 600 11px Archivo, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.09em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-stat-red .ds-stat-top { color: var(--red, #c0303c); } .ds-stat-value { display: block; font: 600 34px Fraunces, Georgia, serif; font-variation-settings: 'opsz' 110, 'SOFT' 24, 'WONK' 1; letter-spacing: -0.02em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums; line-height: 1.08; margin-top: 10px; } .ds-stat-red .ds-stat-value { color: var(--red, #c0303c); } .ds-icon-sm { width: 14px; height: 14px; flex: none; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: The single text-input style used across every form in the system.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 7px; font-family: Archivo, -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-field-label { font: 600 11px inherit; letter-spacing: 0.09em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--fg-secondary, #5b5480); } .ds-input { width: 100%; padding: 8px 12px; min-height: 38px; font: 14px inherit; color: var(--fg, #1a1541); background: var(--bg-field, #fff); border: 1px solid var(--separator-strong, rgba(41,33,104,0.22)); border-radius: var(--r-sm, 5px); transition: border-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), box-shadow 180ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--accent, #292168); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--accent-soft, rgba(41,33,104,0.09)); }

components.name: Accession Slip
components.description: Signature component: a loan/reservation rendered as a card in a paper pocket -- a perforated indigo stub stamping the due date, the record on the right. Restamps coral when overdue, apricot when due soon.
components.html:
Due14Aug
The Great Gatsby
F. Scott Fitzgerald
ACC-2024-00318
components.css: .ds-slip { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 92px 1fr; background: var(--bg-content, #fff); border-radius: var(--r-md, 8px); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(26,21,65,0.07), 0 0 0 1px rgba(41,33,104,0.06); overflow: hidden; } .ds-slip-stub { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 2px; padding: 14px 8px; background: #292168; color: #fff; text-align: center; } .ds-slip-overdue .ds-slip-stub { background: #c0303c; } .ds-slip-stub::after { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; right: -1px; width: 6px; background-image: radial-gradient(circle at 100% 50%, var(--bg-content, #fff) 0 3px, transparent 3px); background-size: 6px 9px; background-repeat: repeat-y; } .ds-slip-stub-label { font: 700 9.5px Archivo, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.11em; text-transform: uppercase; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.46); } .ds-slip-stub-day { font: 600 30px Fraunces, Georgia, serif; font-variation-settings: 'opsz' 110, 'SOFT' 24, 'WONK' 1; line-height: 1; font-variant-numeric: lining-nums; } .ds-slip-stub-month { font: 600 12.5px 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.66); } .ds-slip-body { padding: 14px 16px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 3px; } .ds-slip-title { font: 600 16px Archivo, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -0.012em; } .ds-slip-author { font: 14px Archivo, sans-serif; color: var(--fg-secondary, #5b5480); } .ds-slip-accession { margin-top: 7px; font: 12.5px 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; letter-spacing: 0.02em; color: var(--fg-tertiary, #6f6892); }

components.name: Confirmation Sheet
components.description: Signature component: a native-style modal dropped near the top of the viewport for destructive/consequential actions, always naming the exact record.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-sheet { width: min(420px, calc(100vw - 32px)); background: var(--bg-raised, #fff); border-radius: var(--r-lg, 12px); box-shadow: 0 18px 48px rgba(26,21,65,0.22), 0 0 0 1px rgba(41,33,104,0.08); padding: 24px 24px 18px; text-align: center; font-family: Archivo, -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-sheet-icon { width: 48px; height: 48px; border-radius: 50%; display: grid; place-items: center; margin: 0 auto 14px; background: rgba(247,99,110,0.16); color: #c0303c; } .ds-sheet-title { font: 600 19px Fraunces, Georgia, serif; font-variation-settings: 'opsz' 40, 'SOFT' 22, 'WONK' 1; margin: 0 0 7px; color: var(--fg, #1a1541); } .ds-sheet-body { font: 14px inherit; color: var(--fg-secondary, #5b5480); margin: 0; } .ds-sheet-actions { display: flex; gap: 9px; margin-top: 20px; } .ds-icon-lg { width: 20px; height: 20px; } .ds-btn-danger { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 7px; padding: 7px 15px; min-height: 34px; font: 550 14px inherit; color: #fff; background: #c0303c; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--r-sm, 5px); cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: #a82833; }

components.name: Tab Bar Item
components.description: Signature component: the member (borrower) phone shell's bottom tab -- the rail laid on its side, with the same apricot marker rule and an unread-style coral badge.

components.css: .ds-sidebar-link { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 11px; padding: 8px 10px; border-radius: 5px; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.66); font: 500 14px Archivo, sans-serif; text-decoration: none; transition: background 180ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-sidebar-link svg { color: currentColor; } .ds-sidebar-link:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.10); color: #fff; } .ds-sidebar-link-active { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.16); color: #fff; font-weight: 600; } .ds-sidebar-link-active::before { content: ''; position: absolute; left: -10px; top: 50%; width: 3px; height: 20px; transform: translateY(-50%); border-radius: 0 2px 2px 0; background: #f9b78a; }

narrative.overview:
The whole system is built out of one physical object: a specimen tag, a hand-assigned accession number, a due-date card tucked in a paper pocket. That vernacular is structurally true here, not a skin over generic UI -- a call number, an ISBN, a due date are real identifying data, so they are set in a fixed-width monospace face and aligned in columns rather than left to flow with surrounding prose. The system's signature component, the .slip, is this object made literal: a perforated indigo stub holding a stamped date on the left, the record itself on the right, exactly like a due-date card in a library pocket.

Color works as a status system, not decoration. Indigo (#292168) is the department's own identity color -- it owns the navigation rail in both light and dark appearance, so the app is recognizable at a glance regardless of theme. Coral marks overdue, apricot marks due-soon, aqua marks available/returned: three brand tints doing the job a generic red/yellow/green traffic light would do elsewhere, except these three are the institution's own palette, reused rather than invented. Every one of these pairings -- and every neutral pairing beside it -- was checked against real WCAG contrast math, in both appearances independently.

The system is self-contained by construction: Fraunces, Archivo, and IBM Plex Mono are all served from static/fonts, every icon is inline SVG, and nothing depends on a CDN. This isn't an aesthetic choice -- it's what lets the accession-slip vernacular render identically on a restricted campus network or fully offline, which is the actual operating condition for a school library. Two sibling shells share this one system without diverging from it: the librarian's circulation desk is dense and desktop-only, while the borrower's side collapses to a phone shell with a bottom tab bar built from the same rail tokens, just laid on its side.
keyCharacteristics: The accession slip (.slip/.slip-stub) as the system's signature component and the source of its whole vernacular -- monospace data in fixed columns, brand color as status
A single saturated indigo field (the rail) that never changes between light and dark appearance, anchoring identity
Brand color used as meaning only: coral/apricot/aqua map to overdue/due-soon/available, never to decoration
Two depth languages: soft ambient ink-tinted shadows for resting content, frosted glass strictly for floating chrome
Full light/dark appearance parity, every token independently re-picked and re-verified against WCAG, never inverted or dimmed
Fraunces at large optical sizes for numbers and page titles -- the one place display type is allowed to be expressive; Archivo and Plex Mono keep everything else quiet and legible

rules.name: The Text/Fill Split Rule
rules.body: --accent/--accent-fill (and --red/--red-fill) are two separate tokens because a value tuned to be legible as text on a dark surface is too light to hold white text as a button or stub fill. In light mode both halves share one value; in dark mode they diverge. Never use the text-tuned token as a background holding white text, or the fill-tuned token as page text.

rules.name: The Independent-Mode Rule
rules.body: Dark appearance ("midnight") is never filter: invert() or a flat opacity dim -- every token is re-derived by hand for the indigo-toned dark ground it sits on and checked against the same WCAG math as light mode ("paper").

rules.name: The Cool-Is-Inventory Rule
rules.body: In a row of summary tiles, the cool lanes (indigo, aqua, violet) color only the number -- they carry counts of what exists. Coral is the one lane that also tints its label, because it's the count that means something is wrong.

rules.name: The Tertiary-Is-Not-Data Rule
rules.body: --fg-tertiary is for placeholders, disabled controls, and decorative icon fills. A real value -- a zero count, an absent date, a row explanation -- is data however unremarkable, and takes --fg-secondary instead.

rules.name: The One-Heading Rule
rules.body: Exactly one real h1 exists per page (the toolbar title); the member phone shell's larger decorative title is aria-hidden and purely visual.

rules.name: The Data-Is-Monospace Rule
rules.body: Any string that is a real identifier -- an ISBN, a call number, an accession line, a due date, a count -- is set in --font-mono with tabular-nums, never left in the body face.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Paper Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow value is tinted with the brand indigo (or deepened toward black with a subtle white-tinted ring in dark mode) rather than neutral black -- a stacked surface reads as belonging to this palette even in its shadow.

rules.name: The Glass-Is-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Frosted-glass blur is reserved for floating navigational/overlay chrome -- the sticky toolbar, the account menu, confirmation-sheet backdrops, the round glass icon buttons -- never for resting content surfaces.

rules.name: The No-Blur Fallback Rule
rules.body: Every backdrop-filter use ships an @supports not fallback to a flat, opaque surface color -- never a transparent layer with no blur.

rules.name: The Explain-the-Block Rule
rules.body: When a control is disabled or an action is unavailable, the interface surfaces the specific reason as copy near the control rather than leaving a silently disabled button.

dos: Do keep color meaning-only: indigo for identity/selection/primary, coral/apricot/aqua for overdue/due-soon/available -- never decorative color blocking on a neutral surface.
Do re-derive every color independently for dark appearance and verify it against real WCAG contrast math; never dim or invert.
Do set any real identifying data -- ISBN, call number, accession line, due date, count -- in --font-mono with tabular numerals, never in the body face.
Do use frosted-glass blur only for floating/overlay chrome, and always ship a flat, opaque @supports not fallback.
Do tint shadows with the brand indigo rather than neutral black -- depth in this system stays "ink," never generic Material grey.
Do collapse all motion under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce -- every transition in this system already does.
Do keep the librarian (admin) shell desktop-only and the borrower (member) shell phone-optimized; treat them as two shells sharing one token set, not one responsive layout.
Do name the exact record in any destructive-action confirmation sheet.
donts: Don't introduce a second brand accent alongside indigo -- Muted Violet exists specifically as the roster/people lane and is not an invitation to add a second "brand" color.
Don't use --fg-tertiary for a real value; it sits below the AA floor by design.

Don't use a fill-tuned token (--accent-fill, --red-fill) as page text, or a text-tuned token (--accent, --red) as a background holding white text -- they diverge in dark mode and this exact mix-up has already caused real contrast bugs (breadcrumbs, tab-bar labels).

Don't add heavy neutral drop shadows, flat Material-style colorful cards, or ripple/elevation effects -- depth here is either a soft ink-tinted hint or true frosted glass, never a loud generic statement.
Don't disable a control without explaining why next to it.

Don't depend on a CDN, web font service, icon font, or any external asset -- every icon is inline SVG and every font is self-hosted from static/fonts, so the app renders identically offline and on restricted campus networks.
